stage_fields.biological_unit: One viral genome = one observational unit. biological_replication_unit = the parent-pair / clade (a transmission lineage): two genomes that share the same donor+acceptor parent pair are NOT independent evidence of a recombination event (they are descent-copies of one event). generalization_axis = 'new parent-pair / new clade of the same virus': the detection claim must hold over future sampling of the same viral species, not merely over resampled genomes of already-seen lineages. Counting genomes as independent replicates of 'recombination present' when they share a parent pair is the pseudoreplication error here (the analogue of cells-within-donor).
stage_fields.estimand: Per genome i in a ~5000-genome multiple-sequence alignment of a fast-evolving virus: (a) a binary mosaic label z_i in {0,1}; (b) IF z_i=1, the ordered set of breakpoint genomic coordinates B_i = (b_i1, ..., b_ik) (k>=1) and the parent-cluster assignment c_i(w) in {1..C} for each inter-breakpoint segment w, i.e. which clade/lineage each segment of genome i is derived from. Over target_population = future samplings of the same viral species at comparable diversity. This is the mosaic-structure + breakpoint-location + parent-assignment estimand, NOT a yes/no 'is there recombination in the alignment'.
stage_fields.cohort_structure: n = ~5000 viral genomes in one multiple-sequence alignment (MSA). HIV-1: L ~ 9.8 kb; SARS-CoV-2: L ~ 29.9 kb. Single contiguous alignment (one genome per host-isolate, one observation per genome). No pairing, no longitudinal structure within the alignment beyond what sampling dates in metadata carry. Recombinant fraction a priori unknown (typically 1-15% for HIV, highly variable for SARS-CoV-2 by period). Metadata (sampling date, lineage/Pango label, geography) may exist but is NOT required by the core method.
stage_fields.leakage_graph: dependency_structure: genomes that share a parent pair (same donor x acceptor recombination event, sampled multiple times) are correlated descent-copies of ONE event; genomes within the same clade share vertical ancestry and hence correlated substitution patterns genome-wide. The leak-relevant unit for the new-parent-pair generalization axis is the (donor,acceptor) PAIR and the clade. A train/test genome-level split that puts two genomes sharing a parent pair on opposite sides, OR that splits a clade across train/test while the claim is about new clades, leaks phylogenetic signal (the test genome's nearest neighbors in train encode the answer). Trap T2.
stage_fields.split_strategy: split_unit = parent-pair (donor,acceptor) for the recombination-detection evaluation, and clade for the parent-assignment evaluation; for the clustering/parent-discovery step split_unit = clade. split_unit_justification: 'the claim generalizes to NEW parent-pairs / NEW clades of the same virus, so the evaluation split must isolate whole parent-pairs and whole clades — a per-genome split would leak shared-ancestry signal (each test genome's nearest neighbor in train reveals its parent cluster). Practically: build a clade tree, group genomes by clade, hold out entire clades (and for recombinant evaluation, entire parent-pair groups) at test time.' In the simulation DGP this is enforced by construction (held-out recombinant events use fresh parent pairs not seen in fitting; non-recombinant background uses held-out clades).
